_comment: Edit this file to add or modify points of interest. Each POI needs: id (unique slug), name, name_ja (Japanese, optional), book (spring-snow | runaway-horses | temple-of-dawn | decay-of-the-angel), lat, lng, type, description. Types: residence, institution, shrine, district, natural, other.

pois.name: Matsugae Family Mansion
pois.description: The grand Meiji-era mansion of the Matsugae marquis family in Azabu, Tokyo -- a blend of Western architecture and Japanese tradition characteristic of wealthy families of the era. Relevant to: Spring Snow.

pois.name: Ayakura Family Residence
pois.description: Home of the Ayakura family -- a traditional aristocratic household in Tokyo steeped in Heian court culture and classical refinement. Relevant to: Spring Snow.

pois.name: Gakushūin (Peers' School)
pois.description: The Gakushuin (Peers' School) in Mejiro, Tokyo -- an elite institution reserved for children of the aristocracy. Relevant to: Spring Snow.

pois.name: Kamakura
pois.description: The coastal city of Kamakura, former seat of the medieval shogunate and home to Kotokuin (the Great Buddha), Engakuji, and numerous Zen temples. Relevant to: Spring Snow.

pois.name: Gesshuji Convent
pois.description: A fictional Rinzai Buddhist convent set in the hills above Nara. Relevant to: Spring Snow.

pois.name: Nara
pois.description: Nara -- the ancient capital of Japan from 710 to 784 CE, home to Todaiji, Kofukuji, Kasuga Grand Shrine, and the deer park of Nara Park. Relevant to: Spring Snow.

pois.name: Nanzenji Area, Kyoto
pois.description: Nanzenji -- a major Rinzai Zen temple complex in Kyoto's Higashiyama hills, founded in the 13th century on the site of a retired emperor's villa. Relevant to: Spring Snow.

pois.name: Hamarikyu / Shimbashi
pois.description: The Hamarikyu gardens and the Shimbashi district -- part of the social and entertainment landscape of Meiji-era Tokyo. Relevant to: Spring Snow.

pois.name: Osaka District Court
pois.description: The Osaka District Court -- part of the Western-style judicial system established during the Meiji era. Relevant to: Runaway Horses.

pois.name: Iinuma Dojo
pois.description: A kendo dojo in Tokyo. Relevant to: Runaway Horses.

pois.name: Kenshindō Dojo
pois.description: A kendo tournament venue in Tokyo. Relevant to: Runaway Horses.

pois.name: Ise Grand Shrine
pois.description: Ise Jingu -- the holiest site in the Shinto religion, located in Mie Prefecture. The inner shrine (Naiku) is dedicated to Amaterasu, the sun goddess. The shrine buildings are demolished and rebuilt every 20 years in a ritual called shikinen sengu. Relevant to: Runaway Horses.

pois.name: Mount Hiei
pois.description: Mount Hiei -- a sacred mountain on the border of Kyoto and Shiga prefectures, seat of Enryakuji temple, the headquarters of the Tendai sect of Buddhism, founded by Saicho in 788. Relevant to: Runaway Horses.

pois.name: Imperial Palace Grounds, Tokyo
pois.description: The Imperial Palace in central Tokyo -- the primary residence of the Emperor of Japan, located on the grounds of the former Edo Castle. Relevant to: Runaway Horses.

pois.name: Marunouchi District, Tokyo
pois.description: Marunouchi -- Tokyo's central business and financial district, adjacent to Tokyo Station. The Marunouchi Building (Marubiru), opened 1923, was one of Japan's first large-scale office buildings. Relevant to: Runaway Horses.

pois.name: Ginza
pois.description: The Ginza district -- Tokyo's most Westernized commercial boulevard, known in the Meiji and Taisho eras for its brick buildings, department stores, and Western fashions. Relevant to: Spring Snow / Runaway Horses.

pois.name: Miho no Matsubara / Suruga Bay Coast
pois.description: Miho no Matsubara -- a pine-fringed coastal stretch on Suruga Bay near Shimizu, with views of Mount Fuji across the water. A site of classical poetic significance, listed as one of Japan's Three Views. Relevant to: Runaway Horses.

pois.name: Wat Arun (Temple of Dawn)
pois.name_ja: 暁の寺（ワット・アルン）
pois.description: Wat Arun (Temple of Dawn) on the west bank of the Chao Phraya River in Bangkok, with its distinctive porcelain-encrusted central prang rising 70 metres. One of Bangkok's most recognizable landmarks. Relevant to: The Temple of Dawn.

pois.name: Thai Royal Palace, Bangkok
pois.description: The Grand Palace in Bangkok -- the official royal residence of the Thai kings from 1782, containing throne halls, government buildings, and Wat Phra Kaew within its walled compound. Relevant to: The Temple of Dawn.

pois.name: Benares (Varanasi) and the Ganges
pois.description: Varanasi (Benares) on the Ganges in northern India -- one of Hinduism's holiest cities, where the ghats along the riverbank serve as sites of pilgrimage, ritual bathing, and cremation. Relevant to: The Temple of Dawn.

pois.name: Honda's Villa, Gotemba
pois.description: Gotemba -- a city on the southeastern slopes of Mount Fuji in Shizuoka Prefecture, with a direct view of the mountain. Relevant to: The Temple of Dawn / The Decay of the Angel.

pois.name: Karuizawa
pois.description: Karuizawa -- a mountain resort town in Nagano Prefecture, popular as a summer retreat for Tokyo's wealthy since the Meiji era. Relevant to: The Temple of Dawn.

pois.name: Mio Signal Station, Shimizu
pois.description: The Mio Signal Station -- a maritime signal station near Miho no Matsubara on Suruga Bay, overlooking the coast below Mount Fuji. Relevant to: The Decay of the Angel.

pois.name: Honda's Villa, Gotemba (Tōru's Adoption)
pois.name_ja: 本多の御殿場別荘（透の養子縁組）
pois.description: Gotemba -- on the southeastern slope of Mount Fuji in Shizuoka Prefecture. Relevant to: The Decay of the Angel.

pois.name: Gesshūji Convent, Final Visit
pois.description: Gesshuji -- the fictional Rinzai convent in the hills above Nara. Relevant to: The Decay of the Angel.

pois.name: Tōru's Tokyo Apartment
pois.description: Shibuya -- a major commercial and residential district in central Tokyo. Relevant to: The Decay of the Angel.
